description: Maps compliance framework objective categories to service capability prerequisites. Used by compute-applicability-matrix.py to determine which objectives are applicable to the target service before framework mapping begins. Objective IDs use CCMv4 as the reference but the category descriptions are generic enough to match similar objectives in other frameworks.

rules.description: Physical and environmental security of data center facilities
rules.reason: Physical datacenter security is managed by AWS under the shared responsibility model. No customer-deployable platform/infrastructure control can satisfy these objectives for any AWS service.

rules.description: Management and security of user endpoints and devices
rules.reason: Endpoint/device management is an organizational IT control domain. No AWS cloud service control satisfies endpoint management objectives.

rules.description: Personnel security, training, and HR processes
rules.reason: Human resources security controls are organizational processes. No technical AWS service control satisfies HR objectives.

rules.description: Organizational audit programs, policies, and governance processes
rules.reason: Audit and assurance objectives describe organizational governance programs (audit planning, independent assessments, remediation tracking). No platform/infrastructure configuration control implements these.

rules.description: Cross-cloud data portability and interoperability
rules.reason: Cross-cloud data portability objectives are not satisfiable by AWS-native platform controls unless the service exposes a specific portability API.

rules.description: Security of application source code, development, and testing
rules.reason: Application-code security (secure development, SAST/DAST testing, AppSec baselines) is the customer workload responsibility. Platform/infrastructure configuration controls (SCP, Config Rules, CFn Guard, Tag Policies) inspect IAM requests, resource configuration, or IaC templates — never application source code, dependencies, or runtime behavior.

rules.description: Automated secure application deployment
rules.reason: Deploy-time template validation and least-privilege deployment controls support automated secure deployment for any service with CloudFormation/IaC support.

rules.description: OS/software patching, vulnerability scanning metrics, mean-time-to-remediate
rules.reason: Patching and vulnerability-metric objectives apply only when the customer manages OS/software patching. Serverless and fully-managed services (Lambda, EFS, managed AI services) are patched by AWS — these objectives are N/A.

rules.description: Managing vulnerabilities in external libraries and dependencies
rules.reason: External library vulnerability management applies to services where the customer deploys code with dependencies (Lambda with layers, container images). Code-signing mitigations indicate the service has this exposure.

rules.description: Backup verification, DR exercises, and response plan testing
rules.reason: Backup and DR exercise objectives apply only when the service exposes backup, snapshot, or replication APIs that a customer can configure. Multi-AZ alone is NOT backup.

rules.description: Continuity planning, resilience of deployed resources
rules.reason: Multi-AZ placement and redundancy controls are a concrete technical contribution to business continuity planning.

rules.description: BCM policies, strategies, documentation, communication
rules.reason: Business continuity governance (policies, strategies, exercises, communication plans) are organizational artifacts. No platform control implements these.

rules.description: Network isolation, segmentation, firewall, VPC security
rules.reason: Network security objectives (segmentation, defense, environment separation) require the service to have VPC/subnet/security-group placement capabilities.

rules.description: Encryption at rest, key generation, rotation, inventory, algorithm selection
rules.reason: Key management objectives require the service to support customer-managed KMS keys.

rules.description: Encryption policies and procedures (organizational)
rules.reason: Encryption policy governance is an organizational process objective.

rules.description: Key revocation, destruction, activation, suspension, deactivation, archival, compromise, recovery
rules.reason: Advanced key lifecycle objectives are conditional — the service must support CMK to have any key lifecycle exposure. Actual key lifecycle is managed by KMS, so these are at best Supportive for the service itself.

rules.description: Logging who accessed what, activity/transaction logging, access control logs
rules.reason: Access-event logging objectives require the service to generate access/activity logs (CloudTrail data events or native application logs to CloudWatch).

rules.description: Security monitoring, alerting, encryption monitoring
rules.reason: Security monitoring and detection objectives are satisfiable by AWS Config rules (misconfiguration detection) for any service that has mitigations.

rules.description: Logging policies, clock synchronization
rules.reason: Logging policy governance and clock synchronization are organizational/infrastructure-level concerns not addressed by per-service controls.

rules.description: Change management technology, unauthorized change protection, baseline management, deviation detection
rules.reason: Change management objectives are satisfiable by CloudFormation Guard (deploy-time validation) and AWS Config rules (drift detection) for any service with IaC and Config support.

rules.description: Change management policies and procedures
rules.reason: Change management governance (policies, procedures) are organizational artifacts.

rules.description: Quality testing as a change management gate
rules.reason: Deploy-time template validation (CFn Guard) acts as a quality gate on infrastructure changes.

rules.description: Rolling back configuration to known-good state
rules.reason: Change restoration requires the service to have corrective/remediation controls (SSM Automation) or rollback capability.

rules.description: IAM policies, least privilege, separation of duties, role management, authentication, authorization
rules.reason: IAM objectives require the service to have IAM-governable access surfaces (execution roles, resource policies, permission boundaries).

rules.description: IAM policies and procedures, identity inventory
rules.reason: Identity governance objectives (policies, procedures, identity inventory) are organizational processes not addressed by per-service controls.

IAM-03.reason: Identity inventory can be conditionally supported by tagging controls that aid resource attribution.

rules.description: Data protection by design, sensitive data transfer, sensitive data protection
rules.reason: Data protection objectives are satisfiable when the service supports encryption (at rest or in transit) and access control.

rules.description: Data classification, retention, disposal, privacy policies
rules.reason: Data lifecycle governance (classification, retention, disposal, privacy impact assessments) are organizational/workload-level concerns. A resource-configuration control classifies the resource, not the sensitivity of data inside it.

DSP-08.reason: Data privacy by design can be conditionally supported by access-control defaults.

rules.description: Regulatory mapping, compliance reporting
rules.reason: Information system regulatory mapping can be supported by tagging/classification controls that associate resources with regulatory context.

rules.description: GRC policies, risk management, information security programs
rules.reason: Governance, risk, and compliance policy objectives are organizational artifacts.

rules.description: Incident response plans, event triage, forensics
rules.reason: Incident response and event triage objectives can be supported by detective/logging controls that feed the triage process.

rules.description: Incident management policies, contact maintenance, forensic procedures
rules.reason: Incident management governance objectives are organizational processes.

rules.description: Supply chain management, accountability, agreements, compliance testing
rules.reason: Supply chain management objectives are organizational/contractual processes.

rules.description: Internal compliance testing and conformance assessment
rules.reason: AWS Config rules provide an internal-compliance-testing mechanism for any service.

rules.description: Audit log protection, access control over log infrastructure
rules.reason: Log protection objectives can be supported by access controls that restrict who can reach the logged resource surface.
